title: Embeddings & Reranking Discovery - HorizonX
summary: Customer currently runs BM25 on Elasticsearch + custom rerank. Exploring Redwood for embeddings-based reranking and hybrid search. Key concerns: throughput (peak ~500 qps), latency SLO ~ <150ms tail, embedding dimensionality (768 vs 1536), vector DB integration (Pinecone/Weaviate/Milvus), cost tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and SOC2/KMS requirements. Agreed next steps: share pricing and security packet, plan benchmark with 10k queries, follow-up technical deep dive.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-21 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Rossi (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (HorizonX Head of Search), Marcus Nguyen (ML Eng), Aisha Khan (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on embeddings+rerank, hybrid search, workload sizing, security reqs.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Luca, our solutions engineer.
00:08 Priya: Hi thanks, excited to talk. Quick context, we run search on Elasticsearch with BM25 and a small in-house reranker. Looking at embeddings to improve recall and reordering.
00:18 Luca: Great, can you give us rough numbers — queries per second, typical doc corpus size, vector dims you're thinking about?
00:25 Priya: Yeah so corpus is ~120M documents, but our frequently scored corpus is a subset - around 20M; peak QPS about 500 during business hours, baseline maybe 80-120 qps. Tail p95 latency target for user queries is 150ms, but we tolerate longer for async re-ranks.
00:42 Marcus: Our current flow: BM25 retrieve top 200, then a transformer-based reranker re-scores top 20. That reranker is expensive, so we want to move to embed+reregister — sorry rerank — using ANN for initial rerank, then light cross-encoder for final.
00:56 Maya: Makes sense. A couple of common patterns: hybrid retrieval (BM25 first) then embed on candidate set, or full vector-only retrieval. Hybrid tends to be more cost-efficient and preserves recall.
01:10 Aisha: For us data residency and encryption is a must — SOC2 plus KMS for key management. We may need Private deployment if hosted isn't acceptable.
01:20 Luca: Understood. Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated, and Private with VPC and KMS integration. We also have audit logs and IAM/SAML. For throughput at 500 qps do you expect peak short bursts or sustained?
01:34 Priya: Short bursts mostly, like 5-10 minute spikes during product launches. Sustained is closer to 80-120.
01:42 Maya: Ok that helps sizing. For spikes Dedicated with burst pool is typical; Hosted can handle but cost may spike. We can propose a mixed approach.
01:52 Marcus: Question on embeddings: is 1536 dims worth it vs 768? We saw small gains but cost doubles storage and compute.
02:02 Luca: Right, dims are a tradeoff. For many use-cases 768 (e.g., open model variants) gives good performance. 1536 helps with semantic nuance on big corpora; however we also do quantization and dimensionality reduction recommendations per workload — we can test both in a pilot.
02:20 Priya: How does vector DB integrate? We currently use Pinecone for a small team prototype. If we migrate, do you recommend Redwood storing vectors or connecting to existing vector DBs?
02:32 Maya: Both are supported. Redwood can host vectors (we provide optimized storage + caching) or we can point to external vector DBs like Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus. For Dedicated/Private customers we often integrate with in-cluster Milvus or managed Pinecone depending on preference.
02:50 Marcus: Latency-wise, when you do rerank (embed then ANN) what are typical numbers for top-100 -> top-20 flow?
02:58 Luca: On Dedicated GPUs with optimized kernels we see end-to-end rerank 80-150ms for a 2-stage (ANN+light cross-encoder) on top100->20 depending on model size and batch. If you want <150ms tail for interactive queries, we tune batching, KV cache, and use smaller embedding dims or approximate search.
03:18 Aisha: Security — where are vectors stored for Hosted? Are they encrypted at rest and do you support customer-managed keys?
03:26 Maya: Hosted stores are encrypted at rest and in transit; we support customer KMS/HSM for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we can offer CMEK for larger enterprise agreements — we'll include in the security packet.
03:40 Priya: We also need audit trails for compliance and RBAC for team access.
03:45 Luca: We have audit logs, per-route dashboards, and role-based access with SSO/SAML.
03:52 Priya: Cool. Can we talk about index sizes and storage? 20M vectors at 1536 dims — rough calc?
04:00 Luca: Roughly, float32 is 1536*4 bytes ~6KB per vector ~120GB for 20M? Wait math — 6KB * 20M is ~120GB, yes. But we recommend quantization (int8/4-bit) and IVF+PQ to reduce storage by 4-8x. So you may end up ~15-30GB effective.
04:26 Marcus: That helps. What about throughput cost if we host vectors and do online rerank for 500 qps bursts?
04:34 Maya: Cost depends on model size, batch efficiency, and whether you use Dedicated reserved capacity. Hosted per-token and per-embed pricing can get pricey at burst scale; Dedicated reservations reduce unit cost. We'll send two scenarios in the pricing deck.
04:48 Priya: For retrieval quality we plan hybrid: BM25 retrieve 200, embed top 200, ANN -> top 50, then cross-encoder on top 10. Any pitfalls?
05:00 Luca: That's a reasonable pipeline. Watch out for latency stacking; you can run embedding at retrieve time for pre-computed doc vectors and only embed queries at query time. Also consider prefix/KV caching for repeated queries.
05:15 Priya: We precompute doc vectors already.
05:17 Marcus: Another thing: cold-start for new documents — we batch index updates hourly.
05:22 Maya: Sounds fine. For indexing throughput we support streaming and batch ingestion. We'll include recommended indexing rates for Dedicated.

-- 05:30 to 20:00 mid-call deep technical discussion (timestamps every ~30-90s) --
05:30 Marcus: Our cross-encoder is custom fine-tuned; we still want that for final ranking. Ideally we want the ANN stage to be cheap and recall-oriented.
05:40 Luca: Agree. For ANN we recommend IVF+PQ or HNSW depending on dimensionality and update patterns. HNSW is faster for reads but heavier on RAM. IVF+PQ gives better storage efficiency with acceptable latency when well tuned.
05:58 Priya: We'd prefer HNSW for lower latency, but memory usage on our cluster is a constraint.
06:05 Luca: In Dedicated you can right-size the nodes; in Private you control infra. If memory is a concern, IVF+PQ with PQ of 8-16 bytes is a good compromise.
06:20 Marcus: Any success metrics we should track?
06:24 Maya: Precision@10, MRR, latency p95, cost per 1k queries, and percent of queries hitting cached results. We'll add eval suggestions to the benchmark plan.
06:36 Priya: Ok. Can Redwood plug into our existing Elasticsearch pipeline where we use ES as the index and Redwood just serves embeddings/rerank?
06:44 Luca: Yes, you can keep ES for BM25 and do a hybrid call: ES returns doc ids, we fetch doc vectors from your vector store or ours, compute similarity, then we call your cross-encoder. We also have connectors and SDKs for common stacks.
06:58 Priya: Any examples or docs?
07:02 Maya: We'll share the hybrid-search design doc and a demo deck (link in notes).
07:06 Marcus: About benchmarks — what's in the standard benchmark plan?
07:11 Luca: Typical plan: you provide a sample of 10k queries + ground truth labels, we run embeddings of both 768 and 1536 dims, run ANN configs (HNSW vs IVF+PQ), measure recall/precision and latency/throughput on Hosted (representative) and Dedicated. We also test cost estimations.
07:28 Priya: Timeline for that? We want results in 2 weeks ideally.
07:31 Luca: We can run a first pass in ~1 week if data is ready; 2 weeks is safe.
07:36 Maya: We'll ask for the sample dataset and a small SOC2 packet request.

-- 07:40 A brief interlude with background noise and crosstalk, transcription imperfect --
07:40 Priya: (laughs) sorry barking in the background — home office life.
07:44 Maya: No worries.

07:50 Marcus: Also curious about model hosting: do you host the embedding model or do we bring our own?
07:56 Luca: You can do either. Redwood maintains a model catalog (open models we verify). You can use our hosted embeddings or bring a fine-tuned private model in Private/Dedicated. For Bring-Your-Own-Model we support model pinning and custom quant profiles.
08:10 Aisha: For security review we'll need to loop in legal and infra. Is there an NDA?
08:16 Maya: We have a mutual NDA; I'll send it with the follow-up.

-- 08:20 onwards conversation about contract types and pilot structure --
08:20 Priya: If we do a pilot, how do we decide Hosted vs Dedicated?
08:25 Maya: Start with Hosted for fast validation if data residency allows; if you need KMS/CMEK or VPC, Dedicated or Private is the route. Dedicated is typically monthly reserved with burst pools for peaks. We'll propose cost models for both.
08:40 Marcus: Any auto-fallbacks if capacity exhausted? We want graceful degradation.
08:46 Luca: Redwood supports model routing and fallback to cheaper variants or region failover. You can define policies for latency or cost.
08:56 Priya: Great. About integrations — does Redwood have native connectors to Pinecone or do we need to build it?
09:02 Luca: We have connectors and recommend using native API where possible; for Pinecone we have a connector, same with Milvus and Weaviate. For custom stores we can build a lightweight adapter.
09:14 Marcus: On monitoring, does Console give token-level cost breakdown and per-model latency?
09:20 Maya: Yes, per-route and per-model dashboards, traces, and alerting.

-- 09:25 to 22:00 more specifics on cost modeling, example numbers (sketchy) --
09:25 Maya: Example: Hosted embed + token cost might be $X per 1k requests with 768-dim; Dedicated reserved capacity could drop that by ~30-50% depending on commit. We'll include numbers.
09:40 Aisha: We'll need a clear SLA.
09:43 Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA options; Hosted has standard uptime but enterprise SLAs are available with contract.

-- 22:10 Action items and next steps recap --
22:10 Maya: Quick recap — action items: we'll send pricing + security packet, Luca will draft the benchmark plan, and HorizonX will share 10k query sample and schema. Any additions?
22:22 Priya: Also include recommended ANN configs to test for both dims.
22:28 Marcus: Please include expected storage and network numbers for the 20M doc hot set.
22:34 Aisha: And NDA + SOW template if pilot goes forward.
22:40 Maya: Got it. We'll follow up.

37:00 Priya: One last question on index update rates — we index about 100k docs/day. Will that affect choice of ANN?
37:08 Luca: For frequent updates HNSW can be heavier; we usually recommend periodic rebuilds or use IVF with smaller update overhead. We'll note that in the benchmark doc.
37:22 Priya: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
37:25 Maya: Thanks, we'll send notes and next steps.
37:28 Aisha: Thanks all.

End call.
